correctness.rationale: The hub split gives the constant shift of the cycle transfer trace. At z >= -1/4 the trace is positive. For z(theta) = -sec(theta)^2/4, 0 < theta < pi/2, differentiating the trace gives -n*2^(1-n)*sec(theta)^(n+1)*sin((n-1)*theta). The d-1 interior sine zeros exhaust the derivative's degree, so even nonreal multiple roots cannot occur at other parameters. The odd critical points are nondegenerate minima of values -tau, ordered by strictly increasing sec(theta); the even maxima cannot be canceled by t >= 0. The d simple t=0 roots are the cosine zeros before pi/2. At each minimum a conjugate pair leaves, with the double root still counting twice at equality, and no degree change or zero crossing can introduce a new real branch. Dividing the second theta derivative by z'(theta)^2 gives the stated positive P''; the implicit function theorem in sqrt(delta) gives A=sqrt(2/P'') and the O(delta) remainder. Expanding log(sec(theta)) to quadratic order with O(theta^4) gives the fixed-j exponent. An independent recurrence/Sturm spot check gave n=8 counts 4,2,0 at t=0,1/8,1000 and n=7 double-root gcd z+1/3 at t=1/27. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The statement about no other real parameter is read inside the expressly stated t >= 0 scope; negative t can cancel a positive maximum. Finite probes supplement the proof only.
